lesson.text: Quick memory: in 4/4 time, how many beats are in a bar? (4.) Today: syncopation, putting the stress between the beats.
Count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &. The numbers are the beats; the &s fall halfway between them, off the beat.
Syncopation puts claps or stresses where you do not expect them: on the &s, or held across a beat. The music bounces and pushes forward.
The 3 + 3 + 2 pattern x--x--x- from grade 5 is syncopated: its second clap lands on the & after 2, between the beats.
Syncopation came into ragtime and jazz from African American music, which grew from West African rhythms. Scott Joplin (1868-1917) wrote syncopated ragtime such as The Entertainer (1902).
Reggae, from Jamaica in the 1960s, puts its guitar chords on the off-beats. Latin American music, samba and many pop songs are full of syncopation too.
Worked example: x-xx-x-x. Count it: claps on 1, on 2, on the & after 2, on the & after 3 and on the & after 4. Three claps are off the beat, so it feels syncopated.
Try it in the world: stamp 1, 2, 3, 4 with your feet and clap only on the &s. Then clap x--x--x- over your stamps. Next: theme and variations.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then copy: mark every box with a clap. These claps are on the beats.
exercises.hint: Count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & and clap on the numbers.
exercises.explain: The claps are in boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then copy this syncopated pattern: mark every box with a clap.
exercises.hint: Count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &. One clap lands on an &.
exercises.explain: The claps are in boxes 1, 4 and 7.

choices: stressing notes between or across the beats
exercises.explain: Syncopation puts the stress off the beat, between or across the beats.

exercises.prompt: When you count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &, the &s are off the beat.
exercises.explain: True: the beats are the numbers; the &s are halfway between.

exercises.prompt: How many claps in this pattern are off the beat, on an &?
exercises.hint: The beats are boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7; the &s are 2, 4, 6 and 8.
exercises.explain: The claps are in boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7, all on the beat: 0.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then copy: mark every box with a clap.
exercises.hint: Count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & as you listen. Where are the gaps?
exercises.explain: The claps are in boxes 1, 4 and 6.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then copy: mark every box with a clap.
exercises.explain: The claps are in boxes 1, 3, 4, 6 and 8.

exercises.prompt: How many claps in this pattern are off the beat, on an &?
exercises.explain: The claps are in boxes 1, 4 and 7; only box 4 is an &: 1.

exercises.prompt: Which music is famous for syncopation?
choices: a march right on the beat
exercises.explain: Ragtime and jazz are full of syncopation.

exercises.prompt: Scott Joplin wrote syncopated ragtime piano music.
exercises.explain: True: The Entertainer (1902) is syncopated ragtime.

exercises.hint: Look for a clap on an even box, an &.
exercises.explain: x--x--x- claps on box 4, an &; the others clap only on beats.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then copy: mark every box with a clap.
exercises.hint: Count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &. It starts with two claps together.
exercises.explain: The claps are in boxes 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then copy: mark every box with a clap.
exercises.explain: The claps are in boxes 1, 4, 7 and 8.

exercises.prompt: How many claps in this pattern are off the beat, on an &?
exercises.explain: The claps are in boxes 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7; boxes 2, 4 and 6 are &s: 3.

exercises.prompt: Where does reggae usually put its guitar chords?
exercises.hint: Reggae has a bouncy, lifted feel.
exercises.explain: On the off-beats, which gives reggae its bounce.

exercises.prompt: Syncopation came into jazz from African American music, which grew from West African rhythms.
exercises.explain: True: its roots go back to West African rhythms.

exercises.prompt: A drummer stresses beats 2 and 4 instead of 1 and 3. What is this called?
exercises.hint: It is on the back half of each pair of beats.
exercises.explain: Stressing 2 and 4 is a backbeat, heard in much pop and rock.

exercises.prompt: Count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & across 8 boxes. Sort these boxes: on the beat, or off the beat?
exercises.hint: The numbers fall in the odd boxes; the &s fall in the even boxes.
exercises.explain: Counting 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &, the beats land in boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7, and the &s in boxes 2, 4, 6 and 8. So boxes 1, 3 and 7 are on the beat, and 2, 6 and 8 are off it.
